title: Cutting Off Craving
note: Those who have cut off deeds past and future still have this body and its fruit, and old habit can draw the mind back to the senses. That thought is a seed of birth, to be cut off by constant knowledge of the truth.

couplets.plain: They say craving is the seed that yields, for all living things at all times, birth that never ends.
couplets.pm: The books call craving the seed that yields unending birth for all living things at all times. As the body is left, the next deed, the signs of the next state and craving for that state arise in turn. Delusion hides knowledge, and the craving carries the soul there. All religions agree on this.

links.reason: Says what craving is at bottom: the seed from which every life’s births are grown.
Birth is what never ends, and craving is the seed it grows from.

couplets.plain: If you must want something, want not to be born. That comes from wanting to want nothing.
couplets.pm: Knowing that birth is suffering, if you are to want anything, want not to be born. That comes of itself when you want to want nothing. Someone who has seen the endless pain of birth, illness, age and death wants only joy, and craving any small pleasure here is the seed of more birth and more pain.
couplets.sensitive: read cold, wanting not to be born is a wish not to exist

links.reason: Gives the paradox: what opens the way is wanting to want nothing.

couplets.plain: There is no great wealth here to match wanting nothing. Even there, nothing equals it.
couplets.pm: In this world that we see, no excellent wealth equals wanting nothing. And not only here: in heaven, which we only hear of, nothing equals it either. The wealth of humans and of gods each looks low beside something higher, but wanting nothing has nothing above it.

links.quote: no great wealth here to match wanting nothing
links.reason: No wealth here, and nothing anywhere else, comes up to it.
Takes the word wealth from money and hands it to the state of wanting nothing.

couplets.plain: Purity is having no craving. That comes from wanting truthfulness.
couplets.pm: What is called release is having no craving, and that comes of itself when you seek the truth. Release is the soul’s freedom from delusion and other stains, so it is called purity. The truth here is the supreme reality, and seeking it means dwelling on it without a break. Cutting off craving is the direct cause of release.
couplets.note: The Tamil says purity and truthfulness. He takes purity to mean release, and truthfulness to mean the supreme reality.

links.reason: Reduces purity to one thing, having no craving left.

couplets.plain: Those who are called free are the ones free of craving. The others are not free in the same way.
couplets.pm: Those called free of birth are the ones free of craving, its direct cause. Others who have cut away other causes but not this one lose some sufferings by doing so, but they aren’t free of birth as these are.

links.quote: Those who are called free are the ones free of craving
links.reason: Keeps the name of free for those rid of craving and denies it to the rest.

links.quote: The others are not free in the same way
links.reason: Shows everyone else as not free in the same way, for lack of it.

couplets.plain: Craving is what deceives you. To fear it is righteousness.
couplets.pm: Someone may have gained every cause of release up to true knowledge, yet craving can slip in through a lapse, throw him back into birth and ruin him. So fearing craving and guarding against it is the righteousness of renunciation. Guarding means never stopping the practice of seeking the truth.

links.reason: Warns that craving is what deceives you.

couplets.plain: If you cut off craving completely, deeds that never fail you will come the way you want them.
couplets.pm: If you fear craving and can destroy it wholly, the deeds that keep you from ruin come in the way you wish, the way with no strain on the body. Those deeds are the righteous acts of renunciation. Someone who has fully cut off craving needs no other righteousness: all they do is righteousness.

links.reason: Says that with craving wholly cut away, deeds that never fail come as you want them.

couplets.plain: Those without craving have no suffering. Where it exists, suffering comes on and on, without end.
couplets.pm: Those without craving have no suffering to come. Someone with this one cause, even with no other, has all sufferings come endlessly, without a break. The suffering the body already carries was earned earlier, so “suffering” here means what craving earns now. Craving alone is the cause of suffering.

links.quote: suffering comes on and on, without end
links.reason: Piles suffering on suffering upon whoever goes on craving.

links.quote: Those without craving have no suffering

couplets.plain: Destroy craving, the worst suffering of all, and joy goes on unbroken, even here.
couplets.pm: If craving, the great suffering, is destroyed, joy doesn’t break off, not only after release but even in the body. It is the suffering that makes all others seem joys, painful even as it arises. With it gone, the mind stops wavering and stays full. Some read ஈண்டும் as “grows”, and he doesn’t follow them.
couplets.note: ஈண்டும் can mean “even here” or “grows”. The plain reading follows him.

links.quote: craving, the worst suffering of all
links.reason: Calls it outright the worst suffering of all.

links.quote: joy goes on unbroken, even here
links.reason: Offers unbroken joy, and not later but here, to whoever destroys craving.

couplets.plain: If you give up craving, whose nature is never to be filled, that very moment gives you a nature that never changes.
couplets.pm: Craving is never filled: it grows on and on after useless things whose fruit doesn’t last. If you give it up, that act at once gives you a state that stays the same for ever. That state is release, free of elation and worry, of birth, illness, age and death, in joy beyond compare. Sanskrit writers call such a person liberated while living.

links.quote: whose nature is never to be filled

ideaLinks.quote: craving is the seed that yields
ideaLinks.reason: Craving is the seed, and birth that never ends is what it yields.

ideaLinks.quote: That comes from wanting to want nothing
ideaLinks.reason: Not being born comes to the one who wants to want nothing.
Wanting truthfulness is how freedom from craving comes.

ideaLinks.quote: Those without craving have no suffering
ideaLinks.reason: Only those without craving are without suffering, while for the rest it comes on without end.
